target.note: Owner-confirmed manually on 2026-10-26. PTP GetDeviceInfo on the same date observed firmware 23.0.1 and serial prefix XTJ*** with 10 operations and no session. The DeviceInfo model string is generic; the HEG-001 model number and no-modification history remain owner-reported. See research/hardware-observations/2026-10-26-manual.json, research/hardware-observations/2026-10-26-ptp.json, and research/compatibility-matrix.json. Do not update the firmware to verify it.

summary.question: Is there a publicly documented, reproducible, software-only entry point to Atmosphère on an unmodified Switch OLED (HEG-001) running firmware 23.0.1?
summary.answer: No publicly documented, reproducible software-only entry point was found in the reviewed public sources as of 2026-10-26.
summary.scope: Public documentation reviewed on 2026-10-26. This is an absence-of-documented-method finding, not proof that no undisclosed method exists.
summary.documented_route: Hardware modchip (out of scope for this software-only project)
summary.closest_public_lead_note: A real software-only userland/sysmodule chain on Switch 2 system software 23.0.1. The author says it was also tested on Switch 1, but it is not packaged for Switch 1, does not provide kernel or bootROM access, and is not documented on OLED/Mariko 23.0.1.
notes: Firmware compatibility is a separate axis: Atmosphère 1.12.1 and hekate v6.5.4 support 23.0.1, but neither provides an entry point.
The only documented route for patched/Mariko consoles is a hardware modchip, which is outside this project's scope.
The surface matrix records what is publicly documented; it does not claim that any surface is unexploitable.

GameShare is a documented flow in which a nearby device sends data that a system applet on the target parses without the user launching a game. It is recorded as EP-011 / L-006; no public vulnerability exists for it.

field_notes.status: Status of the claim that this surface provides a publicly documented, reproducible software-only path to Atmosphère on the target.
field_notes.public_chain_on_target: Whether a public chain is documented for this exact target: OLED/Mariko hardware on firmware 23.0.1. A surface can have a real public primitive (PARTIALLY VERIFIED) without a target-specific chain.
field_notes.leads_to_atmosphere: Whether the surface, as publicly documented, provides a complete path to launching Atmosphère on the target.
field_notes.software_only: No modchip, soldering, or console hardware modification. An external USB cable, jig, host, or game card is not a hardware modification.
field_notes.physical_access: none, optional, or required. This describes physical access to the console, not whether the method is software-only.

status_legend.meaning: Directly supported by an authoritative or primary source, with no reviewed contradiction.
Indirect evidence, or evidence that covers a related but not identical case.
Plausible or user-reported, but not independently checked.
Contradicted by an authoritative source or direct evidence.
Insufficient evidence; neither supported nor contradicted.

surfaces.name: BootROM / RCM USB recovery
surfaces.description: The Tegra bootROM's USB recovery mode (RCM/APX). On vulnerable Erista consoles, Fusée Gelée (CVE-2018-6242) lets a USB host send an unsigned payload before Horizon OS starts.
surfaces.access_required: Physical: force RCM with a jig or button combination, connect USB, and run a host-side payload sender.
surfaces.status_basis: The OLED uses Mariko/Tegra X1+ hardware, whose bootROM is patched against Fusée Gelée. Patched consoles can enter RCM and enumerate as 0955:7321, but cannot receive the payload.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Unsigned code execution before Horizon OS; the classic route to a custom bootloader and Atmosphère.
surfaces.notes: Do not attempt payload injection on the target. RCM enumeration is not evidence that injection works.

surfaces.name: Recovery / Maintenance mode
surfaces.description: The stock recovery menu entered with Volume Up + Volume Down + Power. It supports system update and initialize/format operations.
surfaces.status_basis: The documented functions are system update and initialize/format. No unsigned-code execution or payload loading is documented.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: None beyond stock recovery functions; it is not a CFW launch path.
surfaces.notes: This describes documented stock behavior. It does not prove the recovery applet has no vulnerabilities, but no public chain was found.

surfaces.name: Browser / WebKit applets
surfaces.description: NetFront NX/WebKit-based applets, including the captive-portal WifiWebAuthApplet and the account-login browser. Historical Switch browser exploits used these applets.
surfaces.access_required: A user-accessible network/applet flow; historical exploits used DNS redirection or a captive portal.
surfaces.status_basis: PegaSwitch is an archived early-Switch toolkit whose documented launch paths target firmware 1.0.0 and the Fake News entry point. No public 23.0.1 browser chain was found in the reviewed sources. Browser applets remain a live attack surface.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Userland code execution in the browser-applet context; a kernel or bootROM stage would still be required for Atmosphère.
surfaces.notes: UNKNOWN means no qualifying public chain was found, not that the browser is safe or that no private chain exists.

surfaces.name: PTP / MTP USB album mode
surfaces.description: The stock 'Copy to PC via USB' album mode. It exposes standard PTP operations for identity and media transfer.
surfaces.access_required: A USB cable and the user-enabled album mode.
surfaces.status_basis: Capmtp exposes only PTP operations 0x1001-0x100A. No code execution, shell, ADB, or general-purpose control interface is documented. GetDeviceInfo is read-only identity data.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Identity observation and media transfer only.
surfaces.notes: Useful for verifying model, firmware display version, and serial prefix. It is not an exploit surface in the reviewed documentation.

surfaces.name: Local wireless (ldn)
surfaces.description: Local wireless networking used for nearby multiplayer and local communication.
surfaces.access_required: Adjacent wireless range; no physical access.
surfaces.status_basis: CVE-2026-82079 is a stack-based buffer overflow in local wireless that affects versions before 23.0.0 and is fixed in 23.0.0. The target is reported on 23.0.1. No public 23.0.1 chain was found. H-010 is a new pre-auth hypothesis: on 2026-10-28 a passive capture confirmed the target advertises a Dragon Ball FighterZ LDN network with a readable plaintext NetworkId header. One approved plaintext security-mode-3 host run was inconclusive because the adapter's transmit path was unconfirmed. The owner supplied prod.keys and a 23.0.1 NCA-only dump; the keys decrypt the Phase 1 advertisement (security mode 1, challenge enabled). On 2026-10-28/29 a prod-mode host emitted 373 AES-CTR advertisements whose decrypted fields match the Phase 1 room, but the console reported no rooms after a roughly one-second search, the host logged no JOIN, and the captures saw no console frames. The same-phy capture may include loopback, so RF transmission is not independently confirmed. The macOS directed-SSID scan is invalid because it returns false positives for non-existent 16-byte SSIDs (E-086). The ldn sysmodule has been identified in the owner's local firmware dump as title 0100000000000018, version 0x5c0004b0 (NCA 755bcf33085ed666cbbcf34de83d1cb0.nca). Its meta NCA is readable and confirms the program NCA hash, but the program content cannot be decrypted because the key file stops at key generation 0x14 and the NCA needs key_area_key_application_16. A second approved prod-mode run repeated the test with the console search triggered after the host was advertising; the host again logged no JOIN, the console again reported no rooms, dmesg TX-report failures rose from 4 to 5, and the wrapper's pcap capture failed on a permission error, so there is no valid run-2 capture. The wildcard CoreWLAN BSSID scan is invalid because macOS returned a nil BSSID for every scanned network (E-088). A second monitor-mode receiver, a phone Wi-Fi analyzer that shows hidden BSSIDs, or the CachyOS PC/mt7921e path is required. On 2026-10-29 a third prod-mode run with the fixed wrapper again produced no join and no room; the independent Location Services-enabled scan did not see the host BSSID, although it saw a hidden ambient BSSID on channel 1, and the same-phy captures contained only host frames (E-089). An AP-mode control proved the adapter can transmit at -32 dBm (E-090), while a monitor-mode control showed that monitor-mode injection does not transmit (E-091). Location Services restored real BSSIDs for the independent scan (E-092). The monitor-mode host path is blocked; the next path is AP-mode management-frame injection, hostapd vendor elements, or a different adapter/driver. An approved AP-mode control then sent a test beacon through NL80211_CMD_FRAME and the Mac saw it at -28 dBm in all 12 scans, so the AP-mode beacon half of management-frame injection works (E-094). The remaining AP limit is the vendor action frame: a broadcast non-public action frame is rejected without a station entry (E-093). A follow-up unicast control added a temporary station entry for the console's MAC and submitted five unicast vendor actions with a non-LDN test OUI; all were accepted without a netlink error (E-095). On 2026-10-29 a real LDN unicast run sent 568 valid AES-CTR advertisements and 568 null-SSID LDN beacons with the AP BSSID through NL80211_CMD_FRAME; all requests were accepted, the station entry was removed, and monitor mode was restored (E-096). The console was off/away, so the room appearance and parser reaction were not observed; the run is inconclusive. A diagnostic showed that the driver rejects a broadcast-BSSID action frame with EINVAL, while the same frame with the AP BSSID is accepted (E-097), so the AP path cannot reproduce the original broadcast advertisement exactly. A supervised rerun on 2026-10-29 then made the room TX10LED appear on the console; selecting it produced 2203-0065 immediately, the search screen closed, and the console returned to the game normally. hostapd logged only AP-ENABLED and AP-DISABLED, with no authentication, association, or station event (E-098). The console therefore accepts the AP-BSSID advertisement at the scan layer, but the join failed before hostapd saw an association. The hostapd SSID was TX10LED-TEST with open security, not the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and LDN RSN IE, so the next test must correct the WLAN configuration and add a userspace responder for the custom 0x88B7 authentication exchange. A second supervised run on 2026-10-29 used the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and the LDN RSN IE. The console authenticated, associated with AID 1, and was marked authorized, then disassociated itself with reason_code=8 about one second later. No 0x88B7 request was observed; the monitor saw a 28-byte null-data frame and the AP socket saw a 20-byte ethertype 0x0006 frame. The console showed 2203-0066 after a few seconds and a game popup 'unable to join the room' (E-099). The association response included an RSN IE that the ldn MonitorAP does not send, so the next run omits it. A local control showed that the AP control port rejects 0x88B7 with EINVAL, while the raw authorized-station path transmits it protected with KeyID 0 (E-100). A third supervised run on 2026-10-29 omitted the association-response RSN IE to match the ldn MonitorAP. The console again authenticated, associated with AID 1, and was marked authorized, then sent one 28-byte null-data frame and disassociated with reason_code=8 about 1.4 seconds after association, before any 0x88B7 request. The monitor pcap contained no console data payload frame (E-101). The association-response RSN IE is not the cause. The current host path is negative; the parser hypothesis remains untested.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Potentially adjacent code execution in the ldn context; a kernel or bootROM stage would still be required for Atmosphère.
requires: A Linux host or Linux VM with an adapter/driver that can transmit LDN management frames (AP-mode management-frame injection or working monitor-mode TX), and approval to transmit LDN frames
For retail encrypted LDN, prod.keys; the no-key plaintext path is conditional
An independent receiver (a Location Services-enabled wildcard BSSID scan, a second monitor-mode adapter, or a phone Wi-Fi analyzer)
surfaces.notes: The known public CVE is fixed on the target. UNKNOWN refers to any other public 23.0.1 chain, not to CVE-2026-82079. H-010 is the active pre-auth test: the 2026-10-28 passive capture succeeded; the plaintext-host run was inconclusive; the prod-mode host emitted valid advertisements but the console reported no rooms and did not join; the same-phy capture may be loopback; the directed CoreWLAN scan is invalid. Another active run requires explicit approval. The next check is a wildcard CoreWLAN scan for the host BSSID or a second monitor-mode receiver. The ldn NCA is identified and its metadata is readable; static analysis of the program content is blocked by key coverage (E-083). The repeat run is also inconclusive: no valid pcap, no join, no room, and an invalid BSSID scan. The next independent check must use a second receiver or a phone Wi-Fi analyzer. On 2026-10-29 the fixed-wrapper run 3 again produced no join and no room; the independent scan with Location Services saw a hidden ambient BSSID but not the host BSSID, and the same-phy captures contained only host frames (E-089). The AP-mode control transmitted at -32 dBm (E-090); the monitor-mode control did not appear on the Mac, so monitor-mode injection is broken on rtw88_8822bu (E-091). The next host path must use AP-mode management-frame injection or a different adapter/driver. Location Services now supplies real BSSIDs to the independent scanner (E-092). E-093 records the AP-mode source limit: NL80211_CMD_FRAME can send an AP beacon, but a non-public vendor action frame on an AP interface needs a station entry, so a broadcast LDN action frame is rejected with -ENOLINK. The next AP test needs a unicast vendor action to a known console station or a different adapter/driver. E-094 shows that NL80211_CMD_FRAME on an AP interface can put a test beacon on the air with this adapter. E-093 still blocks a broadcast vendor action frame without a station entry. The next AP test is a unicast vendor action to the console's station MAC, which requires new explicit approval, or a different adapter/driver. E-095 confirms the kernel-level station-lookup half of the AP path with a temporary station entry and a non-LDN test OUI. It does not show that the console received the frame or that its LDN parser reacted. The next AP-mode prod-mode run must use a real LDN vendor action and observe the console, with new approval. On 2026-10-29 a real LDN unicast run sent 568 valid AES-CTR advertisements and 568 null-SSID LDN beacons with the AP BSSID through NL80211_CMD_FRAME; all requests were accepted, the station entry was removed, and monitor mode was restored (E-096). The console was off/away, so the room appearance and parser reaction were not observed; the run is inconclusive. A diagnostic showed that the driver rejects a broadcast-BSSID action frame with EINVAL, while the same frame with the AP BSSID is accepted (E-097), so the AP path cannot reproduce the original broadcast advertisement exactly. A supervised rerun on 2026-10-29 then made the room TX10LED appear on the console; selecting it produced 2203-0065 immediately, the search screen closed, and the console returned to the game normally. hostapd logged only AP-ENABLED and AP-DISABLED, with no authentication, association, or station event (E-098). The console therefore accepts the AP-BSSID advertisement at the scan layer, but the join failed before hostapd saw an association. The hostapd SSID was TX10LED-TEST with open security, not the room's 32-character hexadecimal WLAN SSID and LDN RSN IE, so the next test must correct the WLAN configuration and add a userspace responder for the custom 0x88B7 authentication exchange. The second supervised run moved the failure past scan and association: the console authenticated, associated with AID 1, and was authorized, then left with reason 8 before any 0x88B7 request (E-099). The association-response RSN IE is the leading mismatch; the next run omits it to match the ldn MonitorAP and captures raw frames. The AP control port cannot carry 0x88B7 on this driver; the raw authorized-station path is the response path (E-100). The third supervised run exhausted the current hostapd/AP configuration: omitting the association-response RSN IE did not change the outcome, and no 0x88B7 request was observed. The leading remaining host-side difference is the beacon SSID encoding (hostapd zero-length versus the ldn MonitorAP's 32 zero bytes). D9 is negative for this host path; the next step is static analysis of the ldn NCA with the missing key generation, a different adapter/driver with working monitor-mode TX, or a different surface.

surfaces.name: Bluetooth
surfaces.description: The Bluetooth stack used for controllers and wireless peripherals.
surfaces.access_required: Adjacent radio range; controller pairing or connection.
surfaces.status_basis: Switchbrew lists Bluetooth stack overflows fixed in 15.0.0, 16.0.0, 21.0.0, and 22.0.0. No public 23.0.1 chain was found.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Potentially adjacent code execution in the Bluetooth/hid context; a kernel or bootROM stage would still be required for Atmosphère.
surfaces.notes: Absence of a listed public chain is not proof that the stack is unexploitable.

surfaces.name: Game saves and cartridges
surfaces.description: Save data, game cards, and game-level parsers.
surfaces.access_required: User save files, a physical game card, or a game-specific service.
surfaces.status_basis: The reviewed flaw list's Games section documents game-level infoleaks and anti-cheat issues, not a public save-data or cartridge code-execution chain on 23.0.1. Save editing is not code execution.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Potentially game-context code execution; a kernel or bootROM stage would still be required for Atmosphère.
surfaces.notes: No public chain found. This surface is game-dependent and is not a generic console entry point.

surfaces.name: System services and sysmodules (ns2jb lead)
surfaces.description: Horizon OS system services and sysmodules, including filesystem (fs), bsdsocket, audio, and other IPC services. A userland/sysmodule compromise can run native code with service privileges.
surfaces.access_required: An initial userland primitive, often from a game or applet. ns2jb uses SmileBASIC 4.4.9.
surfaces.status_basis: ns2jb is a real software-only, tethered userland/sysmodule chain on Switch 2 system software 23.0.1. The author says it was also tested on Switch 1 but has not been packaged. It runs native code as ordinary sysmodules and fs, without kernel access, CFW, or persistence. No OLED/23.0.1 test is documented.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Native code as ordinary sysmodules and fs; not kernel, bootROM, or CFW.
surfaces.notes: Closest public lead. It shows that a software-only userland/sysmodule chain can exist on recent firmware, but it does not provide a path to Atmosphère by itself. The Switch 1 test's model and firmware are not stated.

surfaces.name: Kernel / TrustZone
surfaces.description: The Horizon OS kernel and TrustZone. Kernel code execution is typically needed for full system control; a bootROM or secure-monitor compromise is needed for pre-boot CFW.
surfaces.access_required: An initial userland or service primitive.
surfaces.status_basis: The reviewed public flaw list contains no unpatched Mariko software-only boot chain and no public 23.0.1 kernel/TrustZone chain. The 23.0.0 fixes include bsdsocket and audio service issues; 23.0.1 lists only a stability fix.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Kernel-level control; not necessarily bootROM access or persistent CFW.
requires: A boot path for persistent CFW
surfaces.notes: No public chain found. Atmosphère needs a boot path, not just kernel code execution; a kernel exploit alone may not survive reboot or launch Atmosphère.

surfaces.name: Hardware fault injection / modchip
surfaces.description: Physical voltage glitching or a modchip that bypasses bootROM verification.
surfaces.status_basis: The maintained NH Switch Guide documents a hardware modchip as the route for patched/Mariko consoles. It performs CPU voltage glitching to bypass bootROM verification and launch a payload from SD.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: Custom bootloader/CFW launch; the documented route to Atmosphère.
surfaces.notes: Out of scope. No installation instructions, wiring, firmware, or automation are provided.

surfaces.name: GameShare / splay applet (receiver-side remote input)
surfaces.description: GameShare lets a Nintendo Switch 2 host share compatible software with nearby systems. On the receiving system the session is handled by the splay system applet (added in 20.0.0), which connects over ldn local wireless, receives a video stream, and accepts host-supplied metadata including the game NACP and JPEG images during setup.
surfaces.access_required: A Nintendo Switch 2 host running GameShare-compatible software, and a user on the target who starts the GameShare receive flow. Only local wireless is documented for Switch 1 receivers.
surfaces.physical_access: proximity (local wireless); no cable and no console opening
surfaces.status_basis: The splay applet and its data flows are documented, so the surface is real and reachable on a 23.0.1 Switch 1 acting as a GameShare receiver. A read-only review on 2026-10-29 found no public vulnerability, proof of concept, or exploit for splay, the GameShare protocol, or its NACP and JPEG handling, and no post-20.0.0 splay security fix: 23.0.0 changed splay's NPDM and RomFS, while 23.0.1 updated only sdb. Locally, the splay program NCA uses key generation 0x17 and is blocked by the missing key_area_key_application_16; its 0x00 meta NCA is readable and its CNMT matches the program NCA.
surfaces.capability_if_successful: At most applet-level userland code execution in splay, whose NPDM grants StreamPlaySaveData (FsAccessFlag bit47) and a broad IPC service list. Not kernel, bootROM, or CFW.
requires: A user-initiated receive flow on the target
A memory-corruption vulnerability in splay or in a service it drives
surfaces.notes: This is a documented flow in which a nearby device sends data that a system applet on the target parses without the user launching a game. Boundaries: hosting requires a Switch 2, Switch 1 receivers are local-wireless only, the host's AdvertiseData is ECC-verified, and any compromise stops at applet privileges. The 2026-10-29 review found no public splay/GameShare vulnerability or post-20.0.0 splay security fix. The local splay program NCA is key generation 0x17 and cannot be decrypted with the owner's keys; the only key-generation-0x15 program is the Mii editor applet miiEdit, which is not a remote-input surface. This is a surface, not an exploit.

leads.name: ns2jb
leads.what_it_is: A software-only, tethered userland/sysmodule jailbreak for the Nintendo Switch 2 on system software 23.0.1. It runs native code as ordinary sysmodules and as the built-in fs sysmodule.
leads.what_it_proves: A software-only userland/sysmodule chain can exist on recent firmware and can run native code without a modchip.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: It does not provide kernel, bootROM, CFW, or persistence. It is packaged for Switch 2, not Switch 1. The author says the chain was also tested on Switch 1, but the model and firmware are not stated and the Switch 1 version is not packaged.
leads.next_step: Look for an independent report or author statement identifying the Switch 1 model and firmware. Do not treat the Switch 2 package as an OLED method.

leads.name: PegaSwitch
leads.what_it_is: An archived early-Switch browser exploit toolkit. Its documented launch paths target firmware 1.0.0 and the Fake News entry point.
leads.what_it_proves: Browser applets were a viable entry-point surface on early Switch firmware.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: Nothing about firmware 23.0.1, Mariko, or the OLED. The repository was archived in 2021 and documents no 23.0.1 support.
leads.next_step: None for the target. It is recorded to distinguish a historical browser path from a current one.

leads.name: Caffeine
leads.what_it_is: An old software exploit for patched Erista consoles on firmware 4.1.0.
leads.what_it_proves: A software-only path existed on a different hardware and firmware combination.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: Nothing about Mariko/OLED hardware or firmware 23.0.1. The maintained guide places it at 4.1.0 only.
leads.next_step: None for the target. It is recorded to prevent the historical Erista path from being mistaken for an OLED path.

leads.name: CVE-2026-82079
leads.what_it_is: A stack-based buffer overflow in Nintendo Switch local wireless networking, fixed in system version 23.0.0.
leads.what_it_proves: A recent public local-wireless vulnerability existed and was patched.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: No public exploit code was found in the reviewed sources. The target is reported on 23.0.1, so this fixed flaw is not available to it.
leads.next_step: None for the target. Monitor for a 23.0.1-specific ldn flaw, but do not assume one exists.

leads.name: Fusée Gelée
leads.what_it_is: A Tegra bootROM Recovery Mode buffer overflow (CVE-2018-6242) that lets a USB host send an unsigned payload to vulnerable Erista consoles.
leads.what_it_proves: The classic software-only entry point for unpatched Erista hardware.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: Nothing about Mariko/OLED. The bootROM is patched; the console can enter RCM but cannot receive the payload.
leads.next_step: None for the target. Do not attempt payload injection.

leads.name: GameShare / splay receiver
leads.what_it_is: A Switch 2 feature that streams a shared game to nearby systems; on the receiving system the session runs in the splay system applet, introduced in 20.0.0.
leads.what_it_proves: A documented, user-reachable flow exists in which the target parses host-supplied data (NACP, JPEGs, and a video stream) inside a system applet that holds StreamPlaySaveData access.
leads.what_it_does_not_prove: No public vulnerability or exploit exists for this flow. It does not provide kernel or bootROM access. Hosting requires a Switch 2, and Switch 1 receivers are local-wireless only. The local splay program NCA is key generation 0x17 and cannot be decrypted with the owner's keys, so its parser has not been analyzed.
leads.next_step: The 2026-10-29 read-only review found no public splay/GameShare vulnerability and no post-20.0.0 splay security fix. The next useful inputs are a Switch 2 host for a supervised receiver test or a key set that covers key generation 0x17 for static analysis; neither is available. Do not spoof a GameShare host or send crafted data to the console.

fixed_public_flaws.name: Fusée Gelée
fixed_public_flaws.notes: The bootROM patch is a hardware revision, not a firmware update. Patched consoles can still enter RCM.

fixed_public_flaws.name: Local-wireless stack-based buffer overflow
fixed_public_flaws.notes: The CVE record lists affected versions before 23.0.0 and a solution of system update 23.0.0. The target is reported on 23.0.1.

fixed_public_flaws.name: bsdsocket AddrInfo deserialization
fixed_public_flaws.identifier: no CVE identifier in the reviewed source
fixed_public_flaws.notes: Switchbrew 23.0.0 documents a vulnerability fix in the nnSdk AddrInfo deserialization code used by bsdsocket.

fixed_public_flaws.name: audio RequestUpdate validation
fixed_public_flaws.identifier: no CVE identifier in the reviewed source
fixed_public_flaws.notes: Switchbrew 23.0.0 states that audio RequestUpdate now performs additional validation and includes vulnerability fixes.

fixed_public_flaws.name: Bluetooth stack overflows
fixed_public_flaws.notes: Switchbrew's flaw list marks the listed Bluetooth stack overflows fixed in those versions. This is not an exhaustive list.
